segments.text: In this video, we will cover how to streamline  your team's responsibilities using a RACI
matrix. We will explore best practices and walk  through how to build one in Lucidchart. To start,
what is a RACI matrix? It is a project management  tool used to clarify roles and responsibilities
for tasks or deliverables. It ensures everyone  knows exactly who owns what. Why use a RACI chart?
It eliminates ambiguity in project management. It  improves communication and ensures that critical
tasks have clear accountability, leading  to more efficient collaboration. There are
four roles of RACI. R stands for responsible,  the person doing the work. A is accountable,
the person making the final decision. C is  consulted, who provides input. I is informed,
who receives updates. The golden  rule of RACI is that for every task,
there must be only one person accountable. While  many people can be responsible, only one person
makes the final decision. Choose your framework  based on needs. Use RACI for standard projects.
Use RASCI to add support roles when extra help  is needed. Use DACI for decision-heavy projects
needing clear drivers. Avoid common pitfalls and  RACI mistakes. Never assign multiple people as
accountable for one task, and ensure you keep  your matrix updated as the project evolves.
For best practices for creating a RACI matrix,  involve your team early. Keep the matrix visible
in a central workspace and review it regularly  during project milestones. Ready to build your
own? Here is a step-by-step tutorial on how to  create a RACI matrix in Lucidchart to keep your
project on track. Start by opening a new document  in Lucidchart. Add a table to your canvas. List
your tasks in the rows, and your team members  or roles in the columns. Once your grid is set,
fill in the cells with the appropriate R, A,  C, or I labels based on your team roles. Use
formatting to color-code your roles for clarity.  Finally, use the share button in the top right
corner to invite your stakeholders to view or edit  the document, ensuring everyone stays aligned.
